newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Forget race, Australian teenagers worry about drugs.
newsitem.headline: Forget race, Australian teenagers worry about drugs.

text.p: Australian teenagers are far more concerned about unemployment or the danger of drugs than about the country's race debate, according to a newspaper poll published on Friday.
And teenage girls -- bigger worriers than boys on all counts -- are also very worried about the environment.

The survey of 600 teenagers carried out for The Australian national daily showed that less than one in five teenagers was "very concerned" by the issue of Aboriginal land rights now preoccupying Prime Minister John Howard.
About 20 percent were worried about immigration policy, despite a race row sparked by anti-immigration politician Pauline Hanson that has dominated news bulletins.

The poll held little comfort for politicians. Only nine percent of teenagers had a lot of trust and respect for politicians, compared to an 82 percent rating for doctors and 60 percent rating for police.
